T40-20/T40-21); sec.55B-C (deductive and inductive logic; probability1 and probability2 for regular functions, pp.296-305); and the theorems of secs.90-93 on symmetrical m- and c-functions (beyond the definition of symmetry and renaming invariance), each with its exact conditions and worked calculations.

Supply written proofs and prerequisite constructions for every result of the not-yet-presented parts listed for the presentation component (in particular the theorems of secs.90-93 on symmetrical m- and c-functions, the sec.40 limit laws T40-21 as stated by Carnap, and the chapter III results used by them), with their exact language (monadic or relational), number domain, effectivity, consistency, cardinality and choice hypotheses. Separately blocked: Proof of the 1950 sec.110I assertion that c* satisfies the variety-of-instances requirement: Carnap refers it to Carnap 1945, 'On Inductive Logic', Philosophy of Science 12, sec.15 (not held). Existence of m*_inf (or of any specified limit c-function) on general sentences of relational L_inf: no proof exists on the route, Carnap does not assert it outside the monadic restriction of sec.110 (sec.110A, pp.566-567), and limits of arbitrary regular sequences need not exist.
